transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Morris (Redwood SE), Tom Reyes (Redwood CSM); Laura Chen (SylvanCare Head of Procurement), Miguel Alvarez (CISO), Priya Nair (Director ML), Evan Brooks (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick procurement review focusing on MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs (uptime/latency), pricing approvals for pilot, and onboarding steps. Action items captured; security docs requested.

00:00 Samir (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick agenda - MSA/DPA redline review, SLA expectations, pricing and pilot details, and then next steps. if we need to loop legal after this we'll capture the redlines.
00:15 Laura (SylvanCare): thanks samir, appreciate it. we're kinda on a tight timeline - board asked we have vendor contracts signed before the end of may, procurement and security need to align.
00:27 Miguel (SylvanCare CISO): yeah security's the blocker for us. we'll need SOC2, pen test summary, SSO / SAML options, KMS integration details, and clarity on data residency and deletion.
00:40 Jenna (Redwood SE): absolutely - we can share our SOC2 report and a pen test summary. for KMS we support BYOK via AWS KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys in select regions.
00:58 Priya (SylvanCare): when you say private deployments, is that VPC only or on-prem as well? for regulated workloads we might need an on-prem option.
01:12 Jenna: we support VPC-hosted private control plane as standard; on-prem packages exist but those are enterprise engagements - we can scope that, though for the pilot we typically run in a dedicated VPC with strict network egress controls.
01:30 Evan (Cloud Arch): network diagrams - can you share CIDR ranges and peering requirements? procurement wants to know if we need firewall exceptions or proxies.
01:40 Jenna: yes, we'll include network diagrams and minimal required ports. note that for dedicated GPU pools there is an outbound connection to the control plane for telemetry and billing, and we can describe the egress rules.
02:02 Samir: let's jump into the MSA redlines - Laura you mentioned your legal had a few edits?
02:10 Laura: right, primarily around indemnity caps, data breach notification timelines (we want 48 hours), and audit rights for subcontractors. also curious about SLA credits and remedy language, and requirement to have a named security contact.
02:26 Samir: okay on breach notification we typically commit to 72 hours initially, can raise to 48 hrs for enterprise tier with SOC2+ contractual language; indemnity cap is usually tied to annual fees but we can discuss. SLA credits - standard is service credits for downtime beyond 99.9% availability, we also expose per-route latency SLOs, e.g., p95 generation latency targets for host models.
02:50 Miguel: for regulated PHI flows, do you allow encrypted-in-flight and encrypted-at-rest using our KMS? and are there BYOK audit logs?
03:05 Jenna: yes, encryption in-transit and at-rest is supported; BYOK audit logs are available for private deployments and via our logs for hosted (we can push to your logging endpoint). we'll include the KMS integration details in the security pack.
03:20 Tom (Redwood CSM): quick note - we have a standard DPA that aligns with EU and US data protection needs, but we'll accept redlines on data retention and deletion windows. what's your expected retention?
03:31 Priya: for training data we have strict rules - anything labeled PHI must be retained no longer than 30 days unless explicitly consented and must be deletable on request.
03:44 Jenna: understood. our DPA has options to turn off retention and disable model training on customer data for enterprise/private deployments. we'll flag the policy options.
04:02 Samir: okay pricing and pilot - what's your expected volume for the pilot? we usually offer a limited trial with a capped token allotment and monitoring.
04:12 Priya: initial pilot estimate is 10M tokens over 4 weeks, mostly generation and some embeddings for search. if that looks off we can adjust.
04:22 Samir: that's a good size. for that volume we can quote a pilot price and potentially a trial credit. pricing sheet I'll send after this call - includes hosted vs dedicated bandwidth and per-token unit pricing and a projected estimate for dedicated capacity.
04:40 Laura: procurement wants to understand cost predictability - can you do committed monthly minimums or reserved capacity?
04:49 Samir: yes we have reserved capacity contracts (Dedicated) for predictable throughput and commit-based pricing. Dedicated comes with SLA commitments and can be scoped to your throughput profile. We'll outline reserved vs on-demand in the pricing sheet.
05:05 Miguel: SLA specifics - what availability SLA do you guarantee, and are there latency SLOs for p95? we need details for our vendor scorecard.
05:18 Jenna: standard hosted SLA is 99.9% uptime for the inference endpoint; Dedicated gets higher SLOs negotiable in the contract. For latency, we publish p50/p95 numbers per model in our catalog - for instance, a typical open model on a GPU pool might have p95 sub-300ms for short prompts but this varies by sequence length. we'll include model-specific performance profiles in the doc bundle.
05:46 Evan: in the SLA credits, how are downtime windows measured - per-region, per-route? and what's the remediation process?
05:55 Jenna: measured at the route level; credits apply if the route fails SLOs over the billing period. remediation is automatic failover to compatible variants as specified by your routing policy; we can include documented runbooks.
06:18 Laura: on legal, the big asks are: 1) 48-hour breach notice clause, 2) remove punitive indemnity language, lower cap aligned to fees, 3) audit rights for subcontractors.
06:34 Samir: we'll accept the request to discuss 48 hours for enterprise tier; indemnity can be negotiated but typically tied to gross negligence exceptions; we can provide a redline reflecting our enterprise practice.
06:46 Miguel: will there be SOC2 Type II? and when was the last penetration test?
06:53 Jenna: SOC2 Type II is available - last audit completed Q4 2025. Pen test summary from 2025-11; we'll share the report redacted as part of the security pack.
07:05 Priya: one item - can Redwood guarantee no model training on customer inputs for the hosted offering? that's important for us.
07:15 Jenna: by default hosted traces might be used for quality improvements but for enterprise accounts we can opt out and turn off usage-based training; the DPA will include a clause to prohibit training on customer data unless explicitly allowed.
07:30 Samir: from a procurement perspective, what approvals do you need on your side to expedite the MSA?
07:36 Tom: once we have a signed MSA + DPA and a standard SOW for the pilot, our onboarding team can provision a dedicated pilot environment. turnaround depends on signatures but we can provision infra in ~5 business days after countersign.
07:52 Laura: pricing approvals - do you need a PO for pilot or can we start after sign-off?
08:00 Samir: for pilots we often do a limited credit or invoice; if procurement requires PO we accept standard PO process. we'll note that in the pricing doc.
08:12 Evan: about network and logs, can you push audit logs to our SIEM? and what's the retention?
08:20 Jenna: we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure logging endpoints; retention configurable on dedicated deployments; hosted has default retention (90 days) but can be extended.
08:36 Miguel: request to include subprocessor list and a commitment to notify changes to critical subprocessors 30 days in advance.
08:45 Samir: yes we maintain a subprocessors register and will include an attestation and notification cadence in the DPA.
09:00 Priya: technical question - for low-latency inference we might want quantized models; do you support different quantization profiles and can we choose model variants?
09:12 Jenna: yes, our serving runtime supports quantization and model variants can be pinned per-route. we can recommend quant profiles based on your sequence length and throughput.
09:28 Priya: great, we'll want recommendations prior to pilot so we can estimate performance.
09:35 Samir: action items recap - i'll send the MSA redline and pricing, jenna will send security docs, priya/evan send workload profile, laura will coordinate legal review.
09:48 Laura: quick note on timing - we need final redlines by 04-29 and sign-off ideally week of 05-10 to meet board ask.
10:00 Samir: noted. if legal needs a call to walk through redlines we can set one up - typically AE + SE + legal join.
10:09 Miguel: one more question on SLAs and credits - do you provide any financial credits for latency regressions or only availability?
10:18 Jenna: currently credits are primarily for availability; for latency we provide operational guarantees and routing fallback; for contractual financial liability on latency regressions that's negotiable on enterprise deals. we'll note that option.
10:34 Priya: ok that sounds fair. we'll review and come back.
10:40 Tom: final note on onboarding - pilot environment will include telemetry dashboards, per-route cost dashboards, and access to a customer success manager.
10:52 Samir: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc bundle. meeting adjourned.
